items.text: Borrow the airport incident in which one aircraft's taxiing jet blast damaged a different, unoccupied aircraft: the operating transfer is protection of an inactive neighbor from an active user's spillover, not a claim that street sound behaves like jet exhaust. Before funding any voluntary noise barrier on consenting property, the association pays a consultant to compare sound at the intended protected edge and an adjacent previously quiet edge during a representative departure period, without recording voices or identities. Release installation funds only if the proposed placement reduces the first measurement without increasing the second; otherwise revise the placement and repeat the comparison within the same project budget. This makes collateral spillover a veto on a locally successful intervention, rather than simply moving complaints across the alley. Publish only the paired aggregate changes and compare aggregate 311 complaints after 90 days. The association funds measurement and installation within its $12,000 total budget; residents, teenagers and workers acquire no duty, and parking and opening hours do not change.

Borrow the airport's published division of operations into general aviation, air taxi and military categories, rather than its particular percentages. The association pays an analyst to divide existing 311 complaints into coarse activity categories without publishing homes, identities or complaint locations, then reserves separate portions of its remaining mitigation funds in proportion to those aggregate activity shares instead of allowing the loudest public meeting faction to capture the whole budget. It publishes only category totals and funded interventions; it collects no new surveillance. Compare category-level complaints after 90 days. The association bears the analytical cost.

Borrow the post-war conveyance structure in which the airfield was transferred to Suffolk County for civilian use but contained a reversal clause reserving return to military use if ever needed. The association buys a small pool of movable acoustic barriers and sound-absorbing curtains with its budget, then conveys them for the 90-day trial to whichever single noise source the categorized 311 data shows is largest, under a written reversal clause: if the day-45 aggregate complaint data shows a different category has become the largest contributor, the equipment automatically reverts to the association and is redeployed there, with no renegotiation and no resident required to give permission or disclose anything. The borrowed mechanism is what makes this a reversion rule rather than a purchase: the association retains ownership and funds any move, while the recipient accepts a temporary asset instead of a permanent one. Feedback signal: the day-45 and day-90 category-level 311 counts that trigger or execute each reversal. The association bears the purchase, storage and moving costs; recipients bear only placement of equipment on their own property, which is voluntary.

Borrow the airport's single fixed-base operator providing services to its different users. Instead of separate businesses purchasing separate mitigation supplies, the association contracts one paid service operator for the 90-day pilot: it holds a shared stock of portable acoustic curtains and departure-information materials and fulfills voluntary requests from participating sites through a single allocation queue. All participating sites use this common stock and queue for association-funded supplies; the operator cannot reserve stock for one favored venue, and publishes anonymous fulfilled and unfilled request totals so shortages trigger reassignment of returned stock before new purchases. The borrowed single-provider relationship replaces duplicated inventories and competing allocation channels; deleting it removes both the common queue and the pooled-stock constraint. Spending on the operator and stock must fit the association's existing $12,000 total envelope after other commitments. Compare aggregate 311 counts and unfilled-request totals at day 90. The association pays all servicing and transport costs, takes no enforcement authority, and assigns no unpaid work to residents, teenagers or low-wage employees; site participation is voluntary and parking and hours remain unchanged.
